chromotherapy_lineage.ancient: Phototherapy practised in ancient Egypt, Greece, China and India. Egyptians used sunlight and specific colours for healing. Egyptian mythology attributes chromotherapy to Thoth — identified in the Zar research as Djehuti ('Tah-Hooti'), the Scribe, associated with Mercury/Hermes. Hermetic traditions used coloured minerals, stones, crystals, salves and dyes, and painted treatment sanctuaries in shades of colour — deliberate manipulation of the electromagnetic environment, not decoration.
chromotherapy_lineage.pleasonton_1876: Augustus Pleasonton, 'The Influence of the Blue Ray of the Sunlight and of the Blue Color of the Sky' — blue light improving growth of crops and livestock and aiding healing. Sparked the American 'blue glass craze'.
chromotherapy_lineage.babbitt_1878: Edwin Dwight Babbitt, 'The Principles of Light and Color', a 600-page treatise. Understood the ANTAGONISTIC effect of red and blue: RED stimulates sympathetic (fight-or-flight) activity, BLUE stimulates parasympathetic (rest-and-digest). Invented the Chromolume, a stained-glass colour-therapy device.
chromotherapy_lineage.ghadiali_1920: Dinshah P. Ghadiali developed Spectro-Chrome therapy after reading Babbitt in the Theosophical Society library in Bombay. Published a chart of which colours to project onto 22 body regions, at exact times of day set by regional astrological timetables. Theory: the body is oxygen (blue), hydrogen (red), nitrogen (green), carbon (yellow), and sickness follows imbalance among the four.

amica_temple_of_radiance.story: Founded by Ivah Bergh Whitten after a diagnosis of incurable illness. On correlating her life with a certain colour she was reportedly healed with no other explanation.
amica_temple_of_radiance.the_significant_part: There was NO shaman and no one instructing her — in contrast to the Zar religion, where a practitioner identifies which deity/Thread is affecting the person. She independently arrived at what Zar practitioners, Egyptian priests and chromotherapists all held: specific colours interface with specific aspects of the electromagnetic body.

brain_lighting_up.electromagnetic_link: Brain activity is itself electromagnetic — EEG measures electrical activity directly, fMRI measures blood flow driven by it. The brain is an electromagnetic system interfacing with electromagnetic signals.

lunar_and_nighttime.current_biology_2013: Under strictly controlled laboratory conditions with NO light cues, around the full moon: EEG delta activity during NREM sleep decreased by 30%, sleep onset lengthened by 5 minutes, total sleep duration fell by 20 minutes, and melatonin was diminished. Described as the first reliable evidence that a lunar rhythm can modulate human sleep structure.
lunar_and_nighttime.science_advances_2021: Sleep timing synchronises with the lunar cycle in both indigenous Argentine communities AND urbanised Seattle populations — sleep starts later and is shorter on nights before the full moon. The persistence under artificial light suggests a mechanism that may be GRAVITATIONAL rather than purely photic.
lunar_and_nighttime.bipolar: Rapid cycling between depression and mania synchronised with ~15-day semilunar phases, when gravitational pull is maximal at new and full moons. 'Lunacy' derives from the Latin.
